guideTitle: 5 Best Handheld Showers With Long Hoses in 2026
metaTitle: Best Handheld Showers With Long Hoses 2026
metaDescription: Five handheld shower heads with 79 to 80 inch stainless hoses compared on pause buttons, spray modes, filtration and how to manage the extra length.
mainKeyword: handheld shower head extra long hose
introParagraphs: A standard handheld hose is around five feet, which is enough to rinse your shoulders but not always enough to reach your feet while seated, wash a pet in the tub or rinse a shower wall in one pass. The picks here all carry hoses of 79 to 80 inches, which is about six and a half feet, and that extra reach changes what a handheld can do, though it also brings a new problem: slack that has to go somewhere.

The lineup includes the FASDUNT 80-inch with five modes and a pause button, the GwernKB 8-mode head and a GwernKB 7-setting head with a built-in power spray and a stated flow rate, the WHZeffect with an 8-setting power-wash mode and a pause button, and a filtered FASDUNT with eight sprays and an 80-inch hose. Separate replacement hoses in 118 and 120-inch lengths also exist for owners who want to extend a head they already have.

We evaluated each on hose length and material, pause controls, spray settings, filtration and how the head handles with a long hose attached. A long hose is only a benefit if the mount and the head let you manage it, so we looked at those details as closely as the length.

products.name: FASDUNT 80 Inch Handheld Shower Head With Pause Button
products.description:
FASDUNT gives the longest hose among the complete heads here at 80 inches of stainless steel, and pairs it with five clearly labeled spray modes and a pause button on the head. The modes run from misty through rain and massage combinations, selected by rotating the head. The ABS body is light, which matters more than usual when a long hose hangs off it.

The pause button is what makes a long hose practical. When you are seated or lathering, you can stop the flow with your thumb and leave the wall valve alone, so the temperature stays put while the hose lies slack. A light head also means the weight of the stainless hose is the main thing your hand feels, not the head itself.

Compared with the GwernKB bars it has fewer modes and a slightly longer hose, and compared with the filtered FASDUNT it is simpler and has no cartridge to replace. It is the balanced choice for a household that wants a very long hose, a pause button and a manageable list of sprays. A simple hook on the wall at shoulder height gives the head a parking place when you need both hands, and the hose can hang in a loose loop from it.
products.bestFor: A very long hose with simple, labeled controls.
cons: Slack needs managing in a small shower
Fewer modes than the 8 and 9 mode heads

products.name: GwernKB 8-Mode Handheld Shower Head, 79 Inch Hose
products.description:
The GwernKB offers eight spray modes and a 79-inch stainless steel hose, with a button on the handle that the listing says shuts the water off completely when pressed. That means you can pause for lathering without the flow dribbling on. The extra-long hose is described as reaching areas a fixed head cannot, which is exactly the job it is bought for.

Eight modes give variety, but the more useful feature is the full-shutoff pause. Some pause buttons leave a trickle, and one that stops cleanly saves water and keeps the temperature steady. The hose is one inch shorter than the FASDUNT's, which makes little real-world difference.

Compared with the FASDUNT it adds three modes, and compared with the 7-setting GwernKB it has a handle-mounted button rather than a front-face stop. It suits someone who likes choice in spray and wants a pause that fully stops the flow. If you are choosing between the two GwernKB heads, decide first whether a handle button or a front stop feels more natural under your thumb.
products.bestFor: More spray choice with a clean pause button.
pros: Pause button fully stops the water
cons: Eight modes are more than most people use

products.name: GwernKB 7-Setting Handheld Shower Head, 79 Inch Hose
products.description:
This GwernKB variant has seven settings, a 4.5-inch face plate, a built-in power spray and a stop button on the front of the head so you can pause the water while you soap. The listing also gives a flow statement: a maximum of 9.85 liters without the water-saving tablet, with a lower figure when the tablet is in place. It is one of the few listings that gives a number for flow.

A stated flow is useful context for a long-hose head, because a long hose adds some resistance and a restricted head can feel weak at the end of it. Knowing that the head can be run with or without a water-saving tablet lets you choose between volume and saving. The front stop button is placed where a thumb can reach it on the face side.

Compared with the 8-mode GwernKB it has fewer modes and a front stop instead of a handle button, and compared with the WHZeffect it states flow. It suits a buyer who wants numbers on water use and is comfortable with a face-mounted stop. Because the listing mentions a water-saving tablet, it is worth checking whether it is installed when the head arrives, since that changes the feel noticeably.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a stated flow and a water-saving option.
pros: Flow figure is stated on the listing
cons: Front stop button is less natural to some hands

products.name: WHZeffect 79 Inch Handheld Shower Head, 8 Settings
products.description:
WHZeffect lets you switch among eight settings with one hand by pressing a button, and turning the handle to the left converts the head into power-wash modes for cleaning. The listing says the pause button stops the water immediately without dripping, and the hose is 79 inches long. The combination of a long hose and a cleaning mode makes it a good tool for rinsing the tub.

One-hand mode switching is a convenience when the other hand is busy holding a child or a pet. A long hose and a power-wash twist make it easy to carry the head to the tub and clean it after a shower. A claim of no dripping is a strong one, so confirm it in reviews before relying on it.

Compared with the GwernKB heads it adds the power-wash conversion, and compared with the FASDUNT it has more settings. It suits someone who wants the shower head to double as a cleaning tool and values one-handed operation. A head that doubles as a cleaning wand tends to get used more often, which spreads the wear across both jobs.
products.bestFor: Cleaning the tub and shower wall with the same wand.
pros: Pause button stops the water immediately

products.name: FASDUNT Filtered Handheld Shower Head, 8 Sprays, 80 Inch Hose
products.description:
The filtered FASDUNT adds a multi-layer shower filter to the 80-inch stainless hose and offers eight spray settings, including rain, mist, granular water and massage, plus a built-in power wash. The listing says the internal space structure and self-cleaning silicone nozzles concentrate the flow, and that the filter purifies the water. It is the only pick here with a cartridge.

A filter changes the ownership picture. You gain cleaner-feeling water, depending on the media, but you take on cartridge replacements and a little extra resistance, which a long hose already adds to. In a weak supply, that combination can feel soft, so it suits a home with decent pressure.

Compared with the plain FASDUNT it adds filtration, more modes and cleaning, and compared with the WHZeffect it uses a filter instead of a twist-to-clean conversion. It suits a household that wants a long hose and a filter in the same head and will keep up with cartridges. Remember that the filter is the part you will pay for repeatedly, so check the replacement cartridge before you commit.
products.bestFor: A long hose and a filter in one head.
cons: Filter plus long hose can reduce force

buyingCriteria.explanation: The FASDUNT lists 80 inches and the GwernKB and WHZeffect heads list 79 inches, which is about six and a half feet. That reaches your feet from a seated position, covers a pet in the tub and lets you rinse a wall in one pass. In a small stall, though, the slack can drape over a bench or pile on the floor. Measure from the mount to the farthest place you will want to rinse, and plan where the slack goes. Draw the hose path on paper from the mount to the farthest spot you will rinse, and add a foot for slack.

All of these use stainless steel hoses, which resist kinking and twisting better than plain plastic. Stainless also feels sturdier and is easy to wipe. The tradeoff is weight, since six and a half feet of steel pulls on a handheld. A swivel at the connection helps stop the hose from winding up. A swivel connection at the hose end stops the twisting that makes long hoses awkward.

A pause button matters more with a long hose, because you often put the head down. The GwernKB 8-mode and the WHZeffect describe full shutoff, the FASDUNT has an on/off button and the 7-setting GwernKB has a front stop. A clean stop saves water and keeps the temperature steady. A brief drip afterward is normal. Think about who is holding the head, because a light head on a heavy hose tires the wrist less than the reverse.

A long hose gives freedom but leaves the head hanging if the mount is too high or too far from where you stand. Place the bracket where you can reach it with your weaker hand. A second hook, or a bracket at a lower height, helps seated users. Test the position before final installation. If you shower seated, check that the bracket can be mounted low enough that you can reach it without standing.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Head weight with a long hose
buyingCriteria.explanation: A light ABS head, as on the FASDUNT, balances better with a heavy stainless hose than a heavy head would. The weight of the hose is carried by the mount when docked and by your hand when in use. If you have weaker wrists, favor a lighter head. Hold the head with the hose attached to feel the pull. A hose that is too long is easier to cope with than one that is too short, but both are solvable with a hook.

A longer hose adds resistance, and a filter adds more. The 7-setting GwernKB states a flow figure, and the filtered FASDUNT has a cartridge. On a weak supply, the combination can soften the spray. Choose an unfiltered head if your pressure is low. If your supply is weak, skip the filter and accept the slightly smaller spray options.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hose length and build
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the 79 and 80 inch hoses and noted that all use stainless steel. Length was weighed against the practical problem of slack. Swivel connections and kink resistance counted in favor. We aimed to picture each head in a small shower, where slack is the biggest annoyance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pause behavior
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each listing describes its stop: full shutoff on the GwernKB 8-mode and WHZeffect, an on/off button on the FASDUNT and a front stop on the 7-setting GwernKB. A clean pause earned credit. Drip claims were treated with caution. Hose length claims were compared across listings and treated as the key spec for this guide.

howWeEvaluated.title: Head weight and balance
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how a light ABS head balances against a heavy hose and how a heavier head would feel. Weight was weighed for wrist comfort. Lighter heads scored higher for seated use. Where a head offered a cleaning mode, we considered whether the long hose makes it more useful.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spray options and extras
howWeEvaluated.description: Settings from five to eight, power-wash modes and the filtered FASDUNT were compared. We asked whether the extras are useful with a long hose. Cleaning modes were counted as practical. We checked how clearly each listing described its pause behavior, since claims differ widely.

howWeEvaluated.title: Flow transparency
howWeEvaluated.description: Only the 7-setting GwernKB gives a flow statement in the text we have. We credited that and flagged others. A long hose adds resistance, so flow information matters. Since all five hoses are stainless, we weighed the head and controls more heavily than the hose material.

faq.q: How long is a long handheld hose?
faq.a: Standard hoses are around five feet, and the long ones here are 79 to 80 inches, about six and a half feet. That is enough to reach your feet from a seat or a pet in the tub. Longer replacement hoses of about 118 to 120 inches also exist. If you are unsure, test with a tape measure from the valve to your seat and then to your feet, because those two numbers tell you the minimum useful length.

faq.q: Will a long hose reduce water pressure?
faq.a: It adds some resistance, though a stainless hose of this length usually has a minimal effect. A filter adds more. On a weak supply, an unfiltered head may feel better. A hose that kinks at the connection is usually a sign that the swivel is stiff, which a drop of silicone grease can help.

faq.q: Where does the extra hose go?
faq.a: It drapes where the mount lets it. Place the bracket so slack falls toward the drain or hangs against the wall, and use a hook or a second holder if needed. In a small stall, a hook at shoulder height helps. Keep the hose out of the tub when not in use, to avoid it resting in standing water.

It resists kinking and feels sturdy, and it wipes clean easily. It is heavier than a plastic hose. A swivel at the connection prevents twisting. If someone in the household is much shorter, a second hook at a lower height spares them from reaching.

faq.q: Can I add a longer hose to my current head?
faq.a: Often yes, since replacement hoses use a standard half-inch connector and fit most handheld heads. Check the connector size and the thread before ordering. A replacement hose is a way to extend a head you already like. Long hoses are especially useful for bathing a child or pet, because the head can be held close to the body to avoid splashing.

faq.q: Do I need a pause button?
faq.a: It is especially useful with a long hose because you will often put the head down. The GwernKB and WHZeffect list pause buttons, and the FASDUNT has an on/off button. It keeps the temperature steady. Rinse the stainless hose with fresh water now and then to remove soap film, and dry the connectors.
